changes: Replaced older ASRM opinion with2019 committee opinion; separated adhesion surrogate outcomes from pain/obstruction benefit.
Added explicit manufacturer contraindication against wrapping Seprafilm around fresh intestinal suture/staple lines.
Removed fixed thermal-energy/cooling safety rules, universal adhesiolysis20% risk and automatic diversion/peritonitis prohibitions.
Corrected rectal injured-surface/peritoneal-reflection anatomy and reconciled2016EAST with2023WTA selected transanal repair pathway.
Corrected two-case Yee report applicability, trauma observational confounding, presacral drainage versus drainage of established contamination.
Corrected open-abdomen relook to24–48hours and explained missed-injury escalation without waiting for fever or a fixed postoperative day.

notes: Replaced deterministic permanent/progressive injury and universal graft/anastomosis failure with individual tissue assessment; removed fixed fractionation/dosimetry rules and unvalidated molecular-prognosis implications.
Corrected ASCENDE-RT 18.4%/5.2% from alleged stricture to cumulative grade 3 GU toxicity, with treatment and denominator scope.
Added PACE-B 2024 large randomized trial and 2026 patient-reported follow-up; explicitly separated cumulative toxicity, visit prevalence and item respondent denominator.
Added ProtecT 12-year randomized-allocation survivorship evidence, with treatment crossover, earlier RT regimen and changing sexual/urinary trajectories.
Removed RTOG–CTCAE equivalence table, universal retention/IMRT prevalence, UI misattribution of composite HR 2.76, and automatic surveillance cystoscopy language.
Replaced formalin-before-HBOT ladder with CUA severity-based approach, alum renal caution, formalin perforation/upper-tract precautions, and high-risk diversion counseling.

Corrected RICH-ART 2025 design to treated follow-up after crossover, with 39/70 actual five-year, missingness, 9 retreatments, mixed-model estimate and exclusion limits; added original 2019 comparison and qualitative Cochrane 2023 context.
Added EAU 2026 selected EPA/augmentation criteria and functional counseling; corrected Rourke 85.7% whole mixed cohort and Asghar 30/34 ureteral-unit denominator.
Removed extrapolated three-woman female urethroplasty certainty, small-series robotic superiority, universal omental necessity and diversion-referral percentages as general risk.
Corrected 2026 female pelvic-floor review outcome-specific denominators/eligibility; removed nested UUI percentage, unqualified biomechanical indices and unverified NCCN citation claims.
Replaced prophylactic PDE5 preservation claim with RTOG 0831 null preventive tadalafil finding; removed categorical implant infection claim and universal menopause prescriptions.

Identified 20 wrong/unrelated original PMID links among 24 original PMID-linked citations. All 28 intended linked source identities/available abstracts read; three unlinked NCCN entries not verified. Rebuilt bibliography to 19 used sources.

reviewRecords.scope: Complete original 323-line MDX and current 139-line rewritten MDX, including all tables and bibliography, read. sources.scope: Complete nineteen-page consensus text including all11references read in three contiguous chunks, extracted lines1–1009. PDF pages133–151. No separate illustrations or supplements reviewed. Complete primary PubMed abstract and COI also read.
notes: Consensus explicitly acknowledges weak comparative evidence and allows individualized practice; not an evidence-graded operative algorithm.
Physical ISL stages0–III are explicitly defined for extremities; direct genital staging/percentage-volume extrapolation must be qualified.
CDT phase1 reduction and phase2 maintenance; no universal required weeks or genital pressure range. Pneumatic treatment can displace edema into genitalia/proximally; individualized monitoring.
Surgery selection and imaging depend on actual functional vessels, tissue composition and context; early-stage success generalization is chiefly extremity experience.
VLNT donor lymphedema reported; reverse mapping may reduce, not eliminate risk. Combined scar release/compression confounds outcomes.

Excision can serve advanced genital disease; superficial collateral loss, wound problems and recurrence considered. Charles/Thompson approaches generally discouraged when alternatives available; this is not a ban on all modern tailored genital excision.

Specialized liposuction is established for selected nonpitting extremity lymphedema, distinct from cosmetic liposuction; long-term compression remains essential. Do not infer equivalent established genital benefit from limb evidence.
Omental transposition/enteromesenteric bridges described as unproven and discouraged; distinguish this from contemporary vascularized omental node transfer, which is a different operation.
Long-term diuretics discouraged for pure lymphedema; comorbid conditions can justify them. MLD additive volume evidence primarily breast-cancer limbs, not genital cohorts.

sources.scope: Complete nineteen-page consensus text including all11references read in three contiguous chunks, extracted lines1–1009. PDF pages133–151. No separate illustrations or supplements reviewed. Complete primary PubMed abstract and COI also read.
notes: Consensus explicitly acknowledges weak comparative evidence and allows individualized practice; not an evidence-graded operative algorithm.
Physical ISL stages0–III are explicitly defined for extremities; direct genital staging/percentage-volume extrapolation must be qualified.
CDT phase1 reduction and phase2 maintenance; no universal required weeks or genital pressure range. Pneumatic treatment can displace edema into genitalia/proximally; individualized monitoring.
Surgery selection and imaging depend on actual functional vessels, tissue composition and context; early-stage success generalization is chiefly extremity experience.
VLNT donor lymphedema reported; reverse mapping may reduce, not eliminate risk. Combined scar release/compression confounds outcomes.

Excision can serve advanced genital disease; superficial collateral loss, wound problems and recurrence considered. Charles/Thompson approaches generally discouraged when alternatives available; this is not a ban on all modern tailored genital excision.

Specialized liposuction is established for selected nonpitting extremity lymphedema, distinct from cosmetic liposuction; long-term compression remains essential. Do not infer equivalent established genital benefit from limb evidence.
Omental transposition/enteromesenteric bridges described as unproven and discouraged; distinguish this from contemporary vascularized omental node transfer, which is a different operation.
Long-term diuretics discouraged for pure lymphedema; comorbid conditions can justify them. MLD additive volume evidence primarily breast-cancer limbs, not genital cohorts.

reviewRecords.title: Vascularized Lymph Node Transfer (VLNT)
reviewRecords.scope: Complete original 247-line MDX and current 136-line rewritten MDX, including all tables and bibliography, read. Consequential selection, anatomy, operative safety, outcome denominators, study design and evidence hierarchy checked against the individually scoped primary sources; current full read is not independent clinical clearance of every claim.

sources.scope: Complete nineteen-page consensus text including all11references read in three contiguous chunks, extracted lines1–1009. PDF pages133–151. No separate illustrations or supplements reviewed. Complete primary PubMed abstract and COI also read.
notes: Consensus explicitly acknowledges weak comparative evidence and allows individualized practice; not an evidence-graded operative algorithm.
Physical ISL stages0–III are explicitly defined for extremities; direct genital staging/percentage-volume extrapolation must be qualified.
CDT phase1 reduction and phase2 maintenance; no universal required weeks or genital pressure range. Pneumatic treatment can displace edema into genitalia/proximally; individualized monitoring.
Surgery selection and imaging depend on actual functional vessels, tissue composition and context; early-stage success generalization is chiefly extremity experience.
VLNT donor lymphedema reported; reverse mapping may reduce, not eliminate risk. Combined scar release/compression confounds outcomes.

Excision can serve advanced genital disease; superficial collateral loss, wound problems and recurrence considered. Charles/Thompson approaches generally discouraged when alternatives available; this is not a ban on all modern tailored genital excision.

Specialized liposuction is established for selected nonpitting extremity lymphedema, distinct from cosmetic liposuction; long-term compression remains essential. Do not infer equivalent established genital benefit from limb evidence.
Omental transposition/enteromesenteric bridges described as unproven and discouraged; distinguish this from contemporary vascularized omental node transfer, which is a different operation.
Long-term diuretics discouraged for pure lymphedema; comorbid conditions can justify them. MLD additive volume evidence primarily breast-cancer limbs, not genital cohorts.

sources.title: Giant Penoscrotal Lymphedema-What to Do? Presentation of a Curative Treatment Algorithm.
sources.access: Complete abstract, main text, both tables, all five figure captions, all twenty-five references and COI read. Every actual figure panel inspected, including separate Figure 4a/4b.
notes: Nine included operations: four without VLNT, three groin VLNT and two scrotal VLNT. Median 49-month follow-up covers all nine; the two scrotal transfers had 18 and 16 months.

All nine had no observed recurrence, including the four without VLNT. Improved imaging in two scrotal-transfer patients does not establish comparative superiority. A postoperative hydrocele was reported.
The paper proposes an anatomical genital classification, not a validated ISL stage I equals CDT-only algorithm.
